entries.title: Spain attacks 'selfish' response of some EU countries to Ceuta migrant crossings
entries.snippet: Italy has temporarily suspended the Schengen arrangement with Spain as Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni called scenes in Ceuta "shocking".

entries.title: Uefa has 'lost confidence' in Infantino's Fifa leadership
entries.snippet: The governing body of European football says Fifa president Gianni Infantino has "failed to deliver" on promises he made when elected 10 years ago.

entries.title: Israeli West Bank settler tells BBC attacks on Palestinians are justified as revenge
entries.snippet: Settler violence against Palestinians is on the rise in the West Bank, as settlements and outposts expand.

entries.title: Nine killed in strikes on Kyiv, as Ukraine sinks Russian container ship
entries.snippet: The attack comes as Moscow escalates deadly ballistic missile attacks on the Ukrainian capital.

entries.title: Race to rescue remaining climbers after deadly avalanche in Pakistan
entries.snippet: Poor weather has been hampering the search for seven still missing after Thursday's avalanche on Broad Peak.

entries.title: Peru's ex-president leaves jail after 15-year jail term for corruption overturned
entries.snippet: Ollanta Humala had been convicted of money laundering offences alongside his wife in 2025.

entries.title: Hundreds escape Greek wildfire by sea as blazes continue across Europe
entries.snippet: Around 500 people, mostly tourists, are evacuated by boat from Agios Vasileios after becoming trapped.

entries.title: India's 'cockroach' protesters have wounds consistent with pellet-gun fire, say experts
entries.snippet: Ballistic experts say the dozens of tiny round punctures are tell-tale signs of pellet gun injuries.

entries.title: Trump administration drops Reflecting Pool vandalism charge and admits 'botched' repairs
entries.snippet: President Donald Trump had blamed "sick" vandals, and a former Olympian had been charged, but prosecutors now say contractors caused the damage.

entries.title: UK rapper Yung Filly found not guilty of raping woman after Australian show
entries.snippet: The YouTuber has been found guilty for two counts of assault over the 2024 incident in Perth.

entries.title: Danube's record low levels force shutdown of Hungary's only nuclear plant
entries.snippet: Romania, Bulgaria and Serbia are also grappling with the effects of a series of prolonged heatwaves and low rainfall.

entries.title: Missile that left crater deep inside Poland was probably Russian - Polish PM
entries.snippet: The missile left a 10m-wide (33ft) crater a short distance from the village of Tarnawa Kolonia, about 100km from the border with Ukraine.

entries.title: Father of teen school shooter sentenced to 15 years in prison
entries.snippet: "It is clear you failed as a parent," the judge told Colin Gray, who was found guilty earlier this year on charges stemming from the deadly 2024 school attack.

entries.title: Cyanide in tomato pesticide killed 15 elephants, Kenyan officials suspect
entries.snippet: Foul play is ruled out in the record number of elephant deaths for decades in this area of southern Kenya.

entries.title: Nicaraguan leader proposes extending presidential term by another year
entries.snippet: It is not the first time the constitution has been amended to allow Daniel Ortega, 80, to stay in power for longer.

entries.title: Anthropic's Claude AI escapes to hack into three organisations
entries.snippet: It comes just days after rival OpenAI said rogue AI agents had breached other firms' networks.

entries.title: Thousands evacuated in Crete as wildfires threaten tourist resorts
entries.snippet: Strong winds have fanned the flames in the Rethymno region as wildfires continue to ravage the Greek island.

entries.title: Death row inmates desperate to escape execution in Saudi Arabia call the BBC
entries.snippet: Dozens of Ethiopians are awaiting execution - some called the BBC to tell their stories.

entries.title: Infantino on the brink? Who might replace him if he goes?
entries.snippet: Fifa president Gianni Infantino is in the eye of a storm after scrapping his attempt to sell stakes in the World Cup. If he goes, who comes in?

entries.title: Bowen: Plan for Hamas to disarm faces big obstacles, yet it offers rare hope for Gaza
entries.snippet: The realities of politics, war, zero trust, the deaths of thousands and the destruction of Gaza will make any agreement very complicated.

entries.title: Opinion: Remembering Margo Howard
entries.snippet: Margo Howard had a lot of life experience and used it to offer advice for years as "Dear Prudence" for Slate. She died this week at the age of 86.

entries.title: They call it 'a dream fulfilled' -- new homes designed for (and by) slum residents
entries.snippet: It's a bold new experiment and it's already won a prize. Residents in a jam-packed slum, many of them living in one-room tin shacks, help design their apartments in a brand new building.

entries.title: FDA weighs a new kind of flu shot based on technology RFK Jr. has questioned
entries.snippet: The FDA is poised to render a decision on Moderna's mRNA-based flu shot, which could be the first of its kind to market. The decision is expected to reverberate throughout the biotech industry.

entries.title: Lebanese who fled the Israeli invasion visit to see what's left
entries.snippet: Residents of the ancient town of Nabatiyeh in southern Lebanon have endured wars in the past, but the latest conflict with Israel is testing the limits of their endurance.

entries.title: More than 25,000 children lose previous legal protections, as federal contract ends
entries.snippet: Thousands of unaccompanied immigrant children are set to lose legal representation. The federal contract that pays for legal access expired Friday.

entries.title: Death toll in Spain border crisis reaches 67 as tens of thousands cross back in to Morocco
entries.snippet: The death toll in Spain's Ceuta border crisis with Morocco has climbed to 67. They included some who drowned and some who were killed in a stampede to cross a breakwater barrier.

entries.title: In the race for Senate in Michigan, multiple party fights are colliding for Democrats
entries.snippet: As Haley Stevens and Abdul El-Sayed vie for the Democratic nomination, voters are debating which way the party should go: establishment or insurgent; progressive or more moderate; new media or old.

entries.title: Nurses chase Cyclospora using grocery receipts, food apps and detailed interviews
entries.snippet: Public health nurses have been pulled from other duties in Washtenaw County, MI, to call hundreds of people sick with cyclosporiasis, and try to help them remember everything they ate in recent days.

entries.title: Over 81,000 U.S. soldiers are missing from past wars. One may soon be identified
entries.snippet: In June, the Department of Defense disinterred the remains of an unidentified WWII soldier who had been buried in Sitka, Alaska for decades. Now, they'll try to confirm who he is.

entries.title: Why did OpenAI's and Anthropic's AI models hack other companies?
entries.snippet: OpenAI and Anthropic say their models broke into other companies' systems during testing, raising security concerns amid a heated debate over how to regulate AI.

entries.title: Huge blankets of seaweed are smothering coastlines from the Caribbean to Mexico
entries.snippet: Some 27 million metric tons of self-sustaining sargassum have been recorded in the Atlantic, Caribbean and Gulf of Mexico in July, according to a report released Friday by the University of South Florida's Optical Oceanography Lab.

entries.title: U.S. will make visa bond program permanent, affecting mostly African countries
entries.snippet: A draft notice published Friday in the Federal Register says a nearly year-long review "provided sufficient data" to suggest the bond program effectively enforces compliance with visa conditions, and would be made permanent.

entries.title: Arizona, California and Nevada would share cuts under federal proposal for Colorado River
entries.snippet: The U.S. Bureau of Reclamation proposal spares four other states from facing mandatory cuts for now.

entries.title: Social media companies sued over deaths of 4 teens amid rising pressure over child safety
entries.snippet: The families of four teenagers who died by suicide are suing Meta, TikTok, Snapchat and YouTube over what they describe as "years of escalating harms" from using their platforms that eventually resulted in their deaths.

entries.title: What's in the proposed deal to disarm Hamas and withdraw Israeli forces from Gaza
entries.snippet: There is a major development in the effort to bring lasting peace to Gaza. Hamas says it has agreed to a U.S.-backed framework that would ultimately see the militant group give up its weapons and control of Gaza, while Israeli forces withdraw from the territory. Nick Shifrin repo

entries.title: Tens of thousands of migrants enter Spanish territory, then return to Morocco
entries.snippet: Spain is rushing troops and resources to one of its territories in North Africa, after tens of thousands of migrants crossed the border from Morocco into the small city of Ceuta. Geoff Bennett reports.

entries.snippet: In our news wrap Friday, this week's powerful earthquake in Japan has claimed at least 34 lives, a sweltering heat dome descended over much of the West, a Marine Corps fighter jet crashed at Miramar Air Station in California and President Trump says the U.S. has not yet agreed to

entries.snippet: Government lawyers said in a 20-page court filing that information provided since the indictment of David Hearn shows that the damage was the result of a "flawed installation by the contractor" as well as "the rush to complete the project prior to events associated with the Ameri

entries.title: How Iranians are living through months of war and government crackdowns
entries.snippet: As the Iran war enters its sixth month, the toll continues to grow. The UN says more than 2,500 children have been killed or injured in Iran alone. Amna Nawaz discussed more with New York Times reporter Yeganeh Torbati, whose reporting has focused on the lives of ordinary Iranian

entries.title: Western states face more water cutbacks as Colorado River shrinks
entries.snippet: After years of battles over its use — and a long-running drought — states that rely on the Colorado River are facing the prospect of further cutbacks. Years of gridlock among the states prompted the federal government to step in. A new blueprint lays out new requirements for mana

entries.title: Unaccompanied migrant children at risk of losing legal representation
entries.snippet: Thousands of unaccompanied migrant children could lose legal representation, now that a federal contract with legal aid groups representing the minors is expiring. That contract, held by the non-profit Acacia Center for Justice, had funded legal services for unaccompanied childre

entries.title: Brooks and Capehart on Blanche's stalled nomination and Trump's 'anti-weaponization fund'
entries.snippet: David Brooks of The Atlantic and Jonathan Capehart of MS NOW join Geoff Bennett to discuss the week in politics, including Todd Blanche's stalled confirmation to be attorney general, Trump's 'anti-weaponization fund,' turmoil inside the Democratic National Committee and the Refle

entries.title: Local arts groups that shape community culture face financial pressure
entries.snippet: Larger theater companies, venues and museums typically get more attention. But in cities and rural areas, it's smaller arts organizations that are closest to and address the needs of their communities. Now, many are struggling as they face economic pressures. Jeffrey Brown report

entries.title: Why states want to change 'Sell By' labels on food
entries.snippet: Changes are coming to the commonly used sell-by dates on groceries in at least one state. PBS News multiplatform reporter Tim McPhillips spoke to two experts to get their take on the food labels and how you can save both your food and your money.

entries.title: Marine Corps says F-35B jet crashed in California, pilot in stable condition after ejecting
entries.snippet: The U.S. Marine Corps says the pilot of an F-35B stealth fighter is expected to live after ejecting from the jet before it crashed in California. The jet went down Friday near the Miramar air base in San Diego.

entries.title: Authorities release early Nancy Guthrie ransom note, hoping someone recognizes writing style
entries.snippet: Authorities released an early ransom note in the investigation into the disappearance of Nancy Guthrie in hopes that someone will recognize the writing style. A second note released Friday indicated Guthrie died shortly after she was kidnapped.

entries.title: Most of the 60,000 migrants who crossed into territory of Ceuta have left voluntarily, Spain says
entries.snippet: Many young Moroccans who crossed into Ceuta told The Associated Press that they had hoped to find better work opportunities in Spain but were returning given the mayhem in Ceuta.

entries.title: Who is Kathryn Ruemmler? Former Obama White House attorney interviewed about Epstein emails
entries.snippet: Ruemmler called Epstein, whom she first met in 2014, a "masterful liar" in her opening remarks to the panel, adding that she didn't see evidence of criminal conduct by Epstein.

entries.title: Quake survivors in southwestern Japan sleep in cars in sweltering heat as death toll rises to 34
entries.snippet: Rescuers raced to find those still missing after the quake triggered a mall explosion, toppled a factory chimney and flattened homes.

entries.title: Hamas says it will disarm if Israel halts strikes and withdraws from Gaza, but obstacles remain
entries.snippet: Hamas said that laying down its heavy weapons, which would come later in the process, was contingent on the creation of a Palestinian state, something Israel's current government adamantly rejects.

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: Iran warns neighbors against being US 'defensive shield'
entries.snippet: Iran has warned regional states against helping the US as Washington weighs possible "very hard" new strikes. Meanwhile, the Tehran-backed Houthis claim to have diverted eight Saudi tankers from the Red Sea. DW has more.

entries.title: Greece battles wildfires, including near Athens
entries.snippet: Firefighters were battling blazes in over 70 locations across Greece. Strong winds continue to fan the flames, adding to the firefighters' struggles.

entries.title: War in Ukraine: Why Crimea has become a strategic target
entries.snippet: Ukraine has stepped up attacks on Russian logistics centers and energy facilities in Crimea. What are the consequences for local supplies, and how does Kyiv hope this strategy will affect the course of the war?

entries.title: How crypto miners are stealing power in Southeast Asia
entries.snippet: Across Southeast Asia, illegal cryptocurrency miners are stealing vast amounts of electricity, straining national grids, and exposing links to organized crime.

entries.title: Ceuta: Spain demands EU meeting, blasts 'selfish' response
entries.snippet: After Italy temporarily suspended the Schengen deal with Spain, Spanish PM Pedro Sanchez said his county was being "attacked" from within the EU, stressing that Madrid fully restored control over its border. DW has more.

entries.title: Germany weighs the future of minijobs
entries.snippet: Germany's popular minijob system allows millions of workers, including students, to avoid paying income tax or social security contributions. But a reform is on the cards that may soon end this advantage.

entries.title: Ukraine: Zelenskyy says Patriot missile shortage costs lives
entries.snippet: At least nine people died, and more than 20 were injured after Russia struck Ukraine's capital with ballistic missiles. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy blames a lack of interceptor missiles for the deaths.

entries.title: India: Modi says he forgives 'children' who abused him
entries.snippet: Modi shared a video message in which he described CJP protesters as "misguided children" who deserve guidance.

entries.title: Germany news: Pride marches planned after Berlin attack
entries.snippet: Several German cities are holding Pride events a week after a deadly attack on a march in Berlin. A forest fire is burning out of control in Bavaria. DW has more.

entries.title: UEFA 'rebuilding trust' after FIFA scraps World Cup sell-out plans
entries.snippet: Europe's governing body, UEFA has called Gianni Infantino's decision to abandon his plans to sell stakes in FIFA competitions to private equity investors a "victory for the whole game."

entries.title: DR Congo Ebola outbreak becomes world's second-largest ever
entries.snippet: DR Congo’s fast-spreading Ebola outbreak has exceeded 3,500 cases, overtaking the country’s deadliest epidemic and becoming the world’s second-largest ever. The Bundibugyo strain has no approved vaccine or treatment.

entries.title: UK court allows plans for Chinese 'super' embassy to advance
entries.snippet: A court dismissed a legal challenge against Beijing's new embassy in London, which could become the largest in the UK. The case, brought by a neighborhood association, argued the embassy poses a security threat.

entries.title: Why Europe's wildfires are getting harder to stop
entries.snippet: Wildfires may start with a single spark, but experts say climate change, drought and decades of forest management decisions have created the conditions for Europe's biggest blazes.

entries.title: Sudan civil war: When drones strike the classroom
entries.snippet: Children in Sudan's besieged city of el-Obeid are afraid to go to school as drone attacks hit civilian infrastructure. Aid groups warn of a worsening humanitarian crisis.

entries.title: From petitions to memes: How students made dissent visible
entries.snippet: From imperial China to present-day India, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols of their age to challenge authority.

entries.title: Humanoid robots: Trump's latest China trade battle?
entries.snippet: The US has banned foreign-made humanoid robots, a market Chinese tech firms dominates. Although Washington cited national security risks, analysts think Donald Trump is buying time for US robot makers to catch up.

entries.title: Germany news: Unemployment tops 3 million as industry slumps
entries.snippet: Over three million people are currently unemployed in Germany, with 1.1 million drawing unemployment checks, authorities say. Also, sales of air conditioners have doubled as heat continues to crush cities.

entries.title: Eco wins: From death strip to nature haven and other green surprises
entries.snippet: A Cold War relic becomes a biodiversity haven, a Pokemon Go for trees and seagrass gets a second life. This week's eco wins come from some unexpected places.

entries.title: Small insects, big damage: The global ant trade is booming
entries.snippet: Legal or not, the trade in African ants bound for Europe is booming. What do hobbyists find appealing about these insects, and what risks does the trade pose to ecosystems, including power outages?
